segments.en: A rider on a sure-footed pony picks a path along a mountain ridge, wrapped in a thick, patterned wool blanket against the cold wind. Below, the valleys fall away into mist. Lumela, hello, from Lesotho!

Lesotho is known as the Kingdom in the Sky. It sits entirely within South Africa, and all of its land lies high above sea level. Even its lowest point is higher than the lowest point of any other country on Earth.
That height shapes everything. Summers are green and full of thunderstorms, while winters bring frost and snow to the peaks, and there's even a ski slope in the Maluti Mountains.
The people are called the Basotho, and their language is Sesotho. When someone greets you with lumela, you can reply, ke teng, which means I am here, I'm fine.
Look for the Basotho blanket, worn like a cloak by men, women and children. Its bold designs mark special moments, from a boy becoming a man to a wedding or a new baby.
And on many heads you'll spot the mokorotlo, a cone-shaped straw hat with a knot on top. Its shape is said to echo Qiloane, a pointed hill near the old mountain fortress of Thaba Bosiu.

Thaba Bosiu is where King Moshoeshoe the First gathered his people in the nineteenth century and founded the Basotho nation. Its flat top was so hard to attack that it became a safe home for all who came.
Out in the highlands, herders care for sheep, goats and cattle, spending long stretches at mountain posts. The wool and mohair from their animals are among Lesotho's most important products.

Everyday food is simple and filling. Papa, a stiff maize porridge, is eaten with moroho, cooked leafy greens, and sometimes with beans or meat. On cold mornings, a warm bowl of sorghum porridge is welcome.
The Maletsunyane Falls plunge down a sheer cliff into a deep gorge, one of the highest single-drop waterfalls in southern Africa. In winter, the spray can freeze into glittering ice.
Water is one of Lesotho's great gifts. Rivers born in these mountains flow down to the lowlands, and huge dams like Katse store water that helps supply South Africa's cities.
Khotso, pula, nala! That's the national motto: peace, rain, prosperity. Now head down from the mountains in any direction, because all around you, South Africa is waiting.
